items.name: Neutrality
items.description: I provide supervised visitation that is fair and unbiased to every parent, caregiver, and agency, focusing on the child's best interest above all else.

items.name: Safety
items.description: I create a structured, secure environment where children and families can interact without fear, conflict, or pressure.

items.name: Respect
items.description: I treat every family with dignity, listening without judgment and honoring each person's background and culture.

items.name: Advocacy
items.description: I stand up for families in need by helping them access services, understand systems, and feel supported during difficult times.

items.name: Professionalism
items.description: With over 10 years in the mental health field as a Medicaid Provider, I follow high ethical standards, clear boundaries, and consistent procedures in every visit.

items.name: Compassion
items.description: I approach every family with empathy and patience, recognizing that supervised visitation often happens during stressful and emotional times.

items.name: Collaboration
items.description: I work closely with courts, DCF, therapists, and other community partners so families receive coordinated, consistent support.

items.name: Supervised Visitation
items.summary: Court-ordered, DCF-referred, or privately arranged visits monitored by a trained, neutral professional in a structured setting.

items.name: Monitored Child Exchanges
items.summary: A conflict-free handoff between caregivers at a set time and neutral location, so children never witness parental conflict at the transfer.

items.name: Therapeutic & Trauma-Informed Visitation
items.summary: Trauma-informed support for families rebuilding trust after crisis, separation, or a period of no contact — grounded in over a decade of mental health experience.

items.name: Court & DCF Documentation
items.summary: Clear, objective visit notes and reports prepared for family court, DCF case managers, and attorneys on every scheduled visit.

items.question: What is supervised visitation and who is it for?
items.answer: Supervised visitation is a court-ordered, DCF-referred, or privately arranged service where a trained, neutral professional is present during time between a child and a parent or caregiver. It's used when a court, DCF, or the family itself wants a safe, documented, conflict-free way to maintain or rebuild the parent-child relationship.

items.question: Do you take sides between parents?
items.answer: No. A New Day Family Services LLC remains completely neutral and unbiased toward every parent, caregiver, and agency involved. We observe, document, and support healthy interaction — we never advocate for one parent over another.

items.question: What areas of Florida do you serve?
items.answer: We serve families across Northeast Florida, including Duval, Clay, St. Johns, Nassau, and Baker counties.

items.question: Are you a Medicaid provider?
items.answer: Yes. A New Day Family Services LLC is a professional Medicaid Provider with over 10 years of experience in the mental health field.

items.question: How do I get started with a referral or custody order?
items.answer: Reach out through our contact information with your court order, DCF referral, or private request, and we'll walk you through intake, scheduling, and documentation requirements.

items.question: What if a family can't afford the full cost of visitation services?
items.answer: Our Family Visitation Sponsorship Fund, supported by community donations, helps cover fees for families who qualify. Visit the Donate page to contribute or to ask about sponsorship eligibility.

AboutPage.metaTitle: About Us | Our Mission, Purpose & Core Values
AboutPage.metaDescription: Learn about A New Day Family Services LLC's mission, purpose, and core values — a trauma-informed, neutral Medicaid Provider serving Northeast Florida families.
AboutPage.heroTitle: A trauma-informed, neutral partner for {serviceArea} families
AboutPage.paragraph1: The purpose of {name} is to provide neutral, safe, and structured supervised visitation services for families across {serviceArea}. We serve families involved with the court system, the Department of Children and Families (DCF), and private custody cases, giving children a secure place to maintain or rebuild relationships with their parents and caregivers. Our role is not to take sides, but to observe, document, and support healthy interactions while keeping children's wellbeing at the center of every visit.
AboutPage.paragraph2: As a professional Medicaid Provider with more than a decade of experience in the mental health field, we bring a trauma-informed, family-focused approach to every service we offer. We understand that many families seeking supervised visitation have lived through crisis, conflict, or major life changes. Because of this, we use clear guidelines, consistent routines, and calm communication to reduce stress and confusion during visits.
AboutPage.paragraph3: {name} exists to advocate for families in need by offering high-quality visitation services and helping connect them to additional community supports when appropriate. Our goal is to help families move toward stability and healing, one visit at a time, so that children can experience a "new day" of hope, safety, and connection with the people who matter most to them.

CommunityResourcesPage.metaTitle: Community Resources for Northeast Florida Families
CommunityResourcesPage.metaDescription: A curated directory of family court, DCF, legal aid, domestic violence, and co-parenting resources for families across Northeast Florida.
CommunityResourcesPage.intro: Supervised visitation is one part of a bigger support system. Here are trusted, independent organizations that can help with legal questions, DCF matters, safety concerns, counseling, and everyday needs. {name} is not affiliated with these organizations — links are provided as a community service and open to each organization's own website.

resources.name: Duval County Family Court Services
resources.detail: Walk-in family court help, 501 W Adams St, 2nd Floor, Jacksonville, FL 32202.

resources.name: Florida Courts Family Law Self-Help Forms
resources.detail: Free state forms for custody, visitation, child support, and domestic violence — usable without an attorney.

resources.name: Jacksonville Area Legal Aid
resources.detail: Free civil legal help for qualifying families, including family law matters.

resources.name: Florida Department of Children and Families (DCF)
resources.detail: Child welfare, dependency case information, foster care, and family support services statewide.

resources.name: Florida Abuse Hotline
resources.detail: Report suspected child abuse, neglect, or abandonment — available 24/7.

resources.name: Hubbard House
resources.detail: Domestic violence shelter, safety planning, and advocacy serving Northeast Florida.

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
resources.detail: 24/7 confidential support for anyone experiencing domestic violence.

resources.name: 211 Northeast Florida
resources.detail: Free, confidential referral line for housing, food, counseling, and other family support services.

resources.name: Jewish Family & Community Services (JFCS) Jacksonville
resources.detail: Counseling and additional supervised visitation and family support programs in Jacksonville.

CommunityResourcesPage.emergencyNotice: If you or a child is in immediate danger, call 911. This directory is for general information only and is not legal advice.
